overall: The AG found one violation: the Committee failed to respond to an Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business days. Notice, minutes, and intent allegations were rejected; immediate and future compliance ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the September 3 meeting notice topics (minutes review, projects, town forest, grants, New Business) were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of those topics listed on the notice.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the September 3 draft minutes lacked a list of documents used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because these minutes remained in draft form at the time of the complaints, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by creating inaccurate or insufficiently detailed minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to respond to his September 9 Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business days; it responded October 25.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee failed to respond to an Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business days, we find that it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the violations were intentional; the AG considered whether the conduct was knowing or deliberately ignorant.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find no evidence that the Committee acted with deliberate ignorance of the law and where the Committee had not been notified of its obligations prior to the events addressed in this letter, we find that these violations were not intentional.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
